summary: This work demonstrates that focused helium-ion-beam-irradiated YBCO Josephson junctions exhibit nearly ideal AC Josephson behavior across the metal–insulator transition, with clean integer Shapiro steps and negligible higher harmonics in the current–phase relation. By varying the irradiation dose from 1.6 to 3.4 × 10$^{16}$ ions/cm$^2$, the barrier is continuously tuned from SNS (metallic, $R 	hickapprox 0.5$–0.8 Ω) through a crossover at 2.4 × 10$^{16}$ ions/cm$^2$ to SIS (insulating, $R 	hickapprox 6$–12 Ω), revealing qualitatively different oscillation periodicities in Shapiro step response to 18 GHz RF power.
motivation: High-$T_c$ Josephson junctions typically exhibit excess current and higher harmonics in the current–phase relation that corrupt AC response and limit device applications. Understanding how barrier properties govern microwave dynamics across the metal–insulator transition could guide optimization for metrology, detectors, and integrated circuits.
method: FHIB-defined junctions were fabricated on 40 nm YBCO thin films and characterized by four-point transport (I–V, temperature dependence of $I_C$ and $R$) and microwave measurements at 18 GHz. Shapiro step amplitudes versus RF power were fitted with stochastic RCSJ simulations using single-harmonic and third-harmonic current–phase relations.
result: Both SNS and SIS junctions are well described by purely sinusoidal CPR with $	hickapprox 2	ext{%}$ third-harmonic correction maximum; measured maximum step amplitudes are $	hickapprox 12$ µA (SNS at 3.77 mW) and $	hickapprox 2.4$ µA (SIS at 1.5 mW), matching long-junction Kautz theory to within ~14–58%; voltage-normalized oscillation spacings are $	hickapprox 101$ µV (SNS) and $	hickapprox 85$ µV (SIS).
